edges.description: Reduced UGDH activity decreases production of UDP-glucuronic acid from UDP-glucose.
Patient-derived cerebral organoids show impaired proliferation of neural progenitors downstream of reduced UGDH activity.
UDP-glucuronic acid depletion reduces synthesis of hyaluronic acid in patient fibroblasts.
Impaired progenitor proliferation is associated with the human neurodevelopmental and epileptic syndrome through unresolved tissue- and circuit-level intermediates.
Biallelic UGDH disease manifests as developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
Marked developmental delay is part of the universal cohort core phenotype.
Axial hypotonia is part of the universal cohort core phenotype.
Moderate-to-severe intellectual disability is part of the clinical syndrome.
Severe epilepsy is a very frequent component of the clinical syndrome.
Patient cells measure endogenous protein abundance and enzymatic activity.
HA in conditioned media provides a direct UGDH-dependent glycosaminoglycan readout.
Mutant organoids are smaller and contain less proliferative SOX2-positive progenitor zones.
edges.limitations: Replication with additional wild-type and complete UGDH-knockout lines is needed because iPSC differentiation is variable.
